#3416. These 10 New Features Are Coming to iOS 27.3

Apple dropped the first developer beta for iOS 27.3 on Tuesday. While this update isn't as large as iOS 27 proper, it's surprisingly feature-filled for a 0.3 update. This is only a beta, so anything could (and likely will) change before Apple officially launches the update. But, as it stands, iOS 27.3 tests 10 new features—including one feature the company trialed in the previous beta.

Technically, anyone with a compatible iPhone can try out iOS 27.3 right now—assuming you enroll your Apple Account in the developer program. But a word of warning: Betas can be temperamental, and could be risky. As such, I'd recommend avoiding the beta until Apple releases the public beta, which comes after a bit more testing to iron out larger issues. Either way, make sure to make a full backup of your iPhone to a Mac or PC first, as issues with the beta could result in permanent data loss.

With watchOS 27, Apple released "Audio Intelligence," a new set of features for Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4. Audio Intelligence uses the watches' new S11 chip, along with on-device AI and cloud-based AI, to run new features, like Sound Recognition and Shazam (music recognition).

With iOS 27.3, however, the company is now officially testing the other two Audio Intelligence features it originally announced with watchOS 27. First, there's Live Rewind: By double-clicking the watch crown, you can pull up a transcript of the last 15 seconds of a conversation. Siri Recap, on the other hand, displays summaries of conversations you had that day, in case you need a refresher on any chats you might have otherwise forgotten about,

The company generated some controversy when it first announced these two Audio Intelligence features, since, on the surface, it sounds like these new Apple Watches are essentially spying on people all day long. According to Apple, however, that isn't really the case. The company says Audio Intelligence is private, and never records or stores any audio. No speakers are ever identified, and text results (both transcripts and summaries) are deleted automatically after a set period of time unless the user saves them to the Siri app. You can read more about how Audio Intelligence works here.

Despite their claims, I'm sure there will still be strong feelings surrounding these Audio Intelligence features. We'll have to see whether Apple can prove Live Rewind and Siri Recap aren't all that creepy throughout the iOS 27.3 beta process.

iOS 27.3 also introduces app actions for Siri AI. Apple is testing new abilities for Siri AI, including organizing files, planning events, or adding photos to albums. You could ask Siri to organize your Downloads folder, or delete files that haven't been opened in more than a year. You could ask Siri to find a coffee shop you went to last week, or to save an article to your Reading List in Safari. You could ask Siri to check your calendar and set up a time for an event based on when you're free. You can even ask the assistant to schedule, edit, or unsend messages.

For example, you could ask Siri AI to help you plan a trip with your friends. You could ask the AI to put together a themed playlist in Apple Music, schedule a message to a group about an upcoming trip, organize the websites you've been visiting in Safari into a tab group, and, after the trip, ask Siri to move your best photos to your favorites album. These new actions work in the following apps: Calendar, Files, Finder, Journal, Mail, Maps, Messages, Music, Notes, Photos, Preview, Reminders, Safari, Shortcuts, and Weather. Developers can also add Siri AI app actions support to their own apps.

Apple started testing its new Health app with the iOS 27.2 beta, but pulled the redesign before the official release. Now, with iOS 27.3, the new app is back. The new Health app has a health dashboard for the first time, as well as new features like Health Age and movement assessments. It seems to be pulling from some popular competitor services, hopefully, for the better. For more on the new Health app, check out Lifehacker health editor Beth Skwarecki's explainer.

Continuing on the Health track, iOS 27.3 also introduces "Gym Strength." This is a new Fitness+ feature that offers a personalized four-week strength-training plan. You can customize these plans to meet your goals, experience level, and schedule, and they adapt as you progress. You'll get recommendations based on your experience with exercises, reps, and sets, including video demos for exercises. You can access Gym Strength on both iPhone and iPad, and Apple Watches are optional—though you can log your progress with the wearable if you have it.

Vertical tabs have been a favorite among browser aficionados, as they give you more screen real estate in your browser while keeping your tabs off the side. Apple hasn't made the jump—until now. This feature works with iPads running iPadOS 27.3 as well as Macs running macOS 27.3.

Another new Safari feature in testing is "Adaptive Dark Mode." This feature forces websites into a dark theme, if they don't have a native theme of their own. There are third-party apps that can do this, but this is the first time Apple has offered this feature built into Safari.

Apple is also testing new StandBy experiences with iOS 27.3, which were previously only available on the iPhone Duo. When you turn your iPhone sideways while plugged in, you'll find new Analog and Digital Clock faces with new customization options. There's also a new Photos face, with the option to pull images from Shared Albums.

"Reachability" pulls your iPhone's display down towards the bottom of the screen, so you can access items towards the top of the display with one hand. It's a useful feature for those of us with big iPhones, and now, there's no iPhone bigger than the Duo. With iOS 27.3, Apple is testing Reachability for its first foldable phone. It's a bit like the inverse of how Reachability currently works: You can swipe on the left or right side of your Duo's display to shift the other side of the screen towards your current position. If you're holding your Duo in your left hand, a swipe of the left side will pull the right side over to the left, and vice versa.

Apple is also rolling out new languages for Siri AI in iOS 27.3. Now, Apple's smart assistant supports Traditional Chinese, Vietnamese, Turkish, and Norwegian.

If you have an Apple Intelligence-compatible iPad running iPadOS 27.3, you now have access to Siri Mode in Camera. As with iOS, you can open the Camera app on iPadOS to access Siri Mode, and ask Siri about your surroundings.

#3415. iOS 27.3 introduces new iPhone Duo feature for one-handed use

iOS 27.3 beta 1 launched today with a variety of new features, including a big upgrade for one-handed iPhone Duo use thanks to Reachability.

When iPhone Duo reviews first arrived last month, some complained that the extra-wide design of the outer display made it difficult to use one-handed.

At the time, Apple said that it would introduce Reachability via a future software update to help.

Today with iOS 27.3 beta 1, Reachability has officially arrived for iPhone Duo users.

Unlike Reachability on other iPhones, which shifts the screen down vertically, the iPhone Duo version works horizontally.

Once the feature is enabled (Settings ⇾ Accessibility ⇾ Reachability), a short swipe to the side of the screen will shift everything to the left or right, making it easier to reach.

If you’re struggling at all with one-handed iPhone Duo use, iOS 27.3 might make a big difference.

Currently iOS 27.3 is only available in developer beta, but a public beta is expected to launch in the coming days. However, if you’re concerned about bugs or performance issues, we recommend waiting for the launch version. Apple has said that iOS 27.3 will ship to all users next month, with mid-December the most likely window.

#3413. iOS 27.3 expands Siri AI with many new capabilities across Apple apps

iOS 27.3 has just entered beta testing and includes major new features for Siri AI across iPhone, iPad and Mac. The company has unlocked many new capabilities across major Apple apps, like Music, Messages, Safari, Reminders and more.

We are still digging into the beta, but here’s a taste of what new things you can get Siri AI to do:

With the Music app, you can now create playlists and save them to your library, like you can ask it to make you “a playlist for songs for a day at the beach”, and then save it for later.

In Messages, you can now ask it to schedule iMessages to be sent later, edit and unsent messages, as well as respond with emoji reactions. You can compose new Notes with bold, italic, and rich text formatting, organize your Notes folders, and more.

Photos gets a big expansion with new Siri AI capabilities that let you favorite photos, rotate and edit images, and rename people and pets all with your voice.

You can now use Siri AI with the Calendar app to create events featuring invitees, location, video call links and more. And in Reminders, you can now create urgent reminders for the first time with Siri.

In Safari, you can now use Siri to create tap groups from a list of URLs, sort your tabs, clear your history, delete reading list items and more.

Journal support with Siri AI is new for the first time. You can create entries with text transcription, or record audio entries.

There’s also wide support for file and folder management with Siri AI Files integration. You can get file content, create files and folders, send files to the trash, organize by type, rename files, and more, using just your voice.

We are also seeing new Siri features for Weather, Maps, Preview and Shortcuts, and will keep testing to find new integrations. Apple is also opening up this support to third-party developers.

iOS 27.3 is currently in beta testing and will be released publicly later this year.

#3410. Developers can now create advanced ‘app skills’ for Siri AI

Apple today announced a major new Siri AI initiative for third-party developers, allowing any app to create Siri AI integrations for the first time. The first versions of Siri AI were limited to a much smaller set of supported schemas.

The new ‘app skills’ also let apps teach Siri how to coordinate complicated multi-step actions. These features are testable in the iOS 27.3 betas.

The app skills sound very similar to what other LLM-driven AI models offer, enabling richer understanding of complicated tasks.

For example, a flight tracking app skill will be able to cleanly map what app intents Siri should use to service a particular kind of user request; something that the first version of Siri AI was simply incapable of doing.

Of course, Apple itself has also taken advantage of the new Siri AI foundational features, with a significant rollout of new capabilities across Apple’s apps.

Here’s an example of what Siri will be able to do, from the developer documentation:

Siri can find custom content from one app, transfer it to a specified app, and perform an action. For example, somebody might request “Hey Siri, send my favorite sneakers to my partner in name of a messaging app.” Siri finds sneakers that the person added to their favorites, understands who the partner is, finds them in Contacts, then sends the sneaker information to them using the messaging app.

It’s also going to be a lot easier to initiate Siri actions for third-party apps. With the Siri AI Developer Preview, users don’t have to explicitly mention the app’s name in many circumstances. For instance, if a Live Activity for a ride-sharing app is active, Siri will automatically understand that a request to “change the ride address” corresponds to the app driving the Live activity.

This gives you a sense of the kinds of things Siri will be able to do in the future, coordinating more complicated actions across Apple and third-party apps.

The new OS releases are in developer beta right now, but Apple says the app skills support is only an early developer preview and is scheduled to officially roll out in the spring.

#3406. 10 2026 Movies That Are Officially Oscar Contenders

This year, the record-breaking MCU movie Spider-Man: Brand New Day and Christopher Nolan's historical epic The Odyssey headlined the biggest summer of cinema since the COVID-19 pandemic. But the late summer nights are turning to cold winter evenings, and the attention of cinephiles has turned to the biggest event in the film calendar: the Academy Awards.

The glitz and glamor of Oscars night is coming into view, as the 99th ceremony readies to celebrate the best of the past twelve months of film. Scheduled to take place March 14, 2027, at the Dolby Theatre in Los Angeles, next year's Academy Awards will feature all the brightest stars in Hollywood today, with ambitious blockbusters, indie darlings, and even a documentary hoping to earn a coveted Best Picture nomination. But who are the current favorites? Here's a look at 10 2026 movies that are officially Oscar contenders.

The film on everyone's lips, A24's You Can See Everything, might finally make history as the first documentary to earn a Best Picture nomination in 100 years of Academy history. The documentary, co-directed by Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim, explores the days leading up to the incarceration of the infamous Theranos founder, Elizabeth Holmes.

"The year's most original movie will make you question reality," wrote Collider's Samuel R. Murrian in one of countless glowing reviews for this mind-bending documentary. With its viral success helping rocket the film up the box office charts, and with the world stunned by the life-altering contents of this three-hour masterpiece, it's possible that You Can See Everything ​​​​​​won't just earn a Best Picture nomination; it could win the trophy.

One of the defining films of 2026, it would be difficult to find someone who hasn't yet seen Project Hail Mary. This epic Phil Lord and Christopher Miller-directed space story follows Ryan Gosling's Ryland Grace as he leads a one-man mission into the stars to try and save the universe. However, he isn't alone in the dense emptiness of space, as he is joined on his mission by an alien he names Rocky.

A favorite to earn plenty of nominations in technical categories, with lead puppeteer and voice actor James Ortiz potentially in the race for Best Supporting Actor, Project Hail Mary will most definitely make its mark on next year's Oscars. As one of the most critically and commercially successful films of 2026, come March 14, 2027, the world could watch Grace Rocky save Oscars.

Another of the most popular films of the year, Focus Features' Obsession will hope to follow in the footsteps of The Substance and Weapons by becoming this year's horror darling at the Academy Awards. Star Inde Navarrette seems most likely to take home Oscars gold, as she currently ranks as one of the favorites in the Best Actress category for a performance that Collider's Hannah Hunt called "one of the year's best" in her review.

A box office record-breaker, becoming the highest-grossing original horror movie of this century among many more titles, Obsession shocked the world as it overcame the latest Star Wars movie through sheer viral appeal. Curry Barker's breakout is nothing short of a horror masterpiece, as one of the most important visionaries in Hollywood's next era gets off to a flying start.

Although some titles lead the charge during the Oscars race, others perform better under the radar, lurking beneath the competition before surprising cinephiles with several nominations. Right now, it seems like one of the best outside contenders for Academy recognition is Olivia Wilde's The Invite, a remake of the Spanish-language comedy The People Upstairs.

Unfolding like a great play, The Invite takes a simple premise, a single location, and four actors at the top of their game and transforms them into an utterly unmissable comedy. But this comedy isn't without its dramatic flair, with every twist and turn playing out like a hilariously realized thriller. Starring Seth Rogen, Edward Norton, and Penélope Cruz alongside Wilde, The Invite feels destined to earn recognition in writing and acting categories.

If, for the aforementioned Penélope Cruz, Oscar night doesn't equal gold for Wilde's The Invite, rest assured she stands a second chance as part of the ensemble of one of the bookies' favorites. Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi's La Bola Negra is a 155-minute drama inspired by the unfinished work of the same name that explores the connections between three gay men and the pain they endure.

Themes of love and loss in the queer community, as well as the erasure of queer identity, become ever more relevant each passing year, with these topics better represented at the Academy Awards in the process. La Bola Negra is the latest LGBTQIA+ story to receive the Oscars spotlight, as it is deemed a favorite to not just earn a Best Picture nomination, but to win the prize.

When forecasting the Oscars nominees for 2027, it's wise to look back at the historical voting of the often predictable Academy. Both 2021's Dune and 2022's Dune: Part Two received nominations in the Best Picture category, having combined to win eight trophies so far. So, with that in mind, the final installment in Denis Villeneuve's acclaimed trilogy seems destined to pick up a handful of nominations once again.

The ambitious attempt to turn the once-thought "unfilmable" Frank Herbert story into cinematic magic has already been the subject of endless praise from critics. But in his last installment, perhaps it's time for Villeneuve to win in the biggest categories? That's what many sci-fi fans will think, and as December 18 and the consequences of Paul Atreides' (Timothée Chalamet) power inch closer, whispers of a Dune: Part Three Best Picture bid grow.

Andrew Scott has quietly proven to be one of the most consistent actors working today, submitting a fine selection of truly terrific performances over the past few years. Come Oscars night next year, it seems the Sherlock star will finally receive recognition as one of the favorites to take home the Best Actor prize as Ian Charleson in the stunning drama, Elsinore.

Directed by Simon Stone and written by Stephen Beresford, Elsinore looks likely to be the second Hamlet-related film in two years to take home an acting prize at the Oscars, following Jessie Buckley's deserved win for Hamnet. Also like Hamnet, Elsinore looks to be this year's biggest tearjerker, with Collider's Therese Lacson writing, "For god's sake, bring more than just one pack of tissues to the theater," in her review.

In 2023, The Banshees of Inisherin was one of the year's biggest nominees, having earned nods in eight categories. Sadly, it won zero prizes, a fate that Irish filmmaker Martin McDonagh will be hoping to avoid with his latest Academy Award play, Wild Horse Nine. The film follows two CIA agents on a mission from Santiago to Easter Island in 1973, and is packed with all of McDonagh's typical dark, comedic wit.

As usual, a McDonagh movie looks set to take home nominations in writing categories, with star John Malkovich heavily tipped to take on the aforementioned Scott for Best Actor. Sam Rockwell, Steve Buscemi, Parker Posey, and the rest of the supporting cast deserve just as much credit for this uniquely encapsulating effort from an unstoppable filmmaker.

It's rare that any given year's Palme d'Or winner doesn't make an impact at the Academy Awards. In recent years, the likes of Bong Joon Ho's Parasite and Sean Baker's Anora have won both Cannes' biggest prize and the Best Picture trophy, so it's fair to assume that Cristian Mungiu's Fjord will also make its presence known come Oscar nominations day.

Mungiu's second Palme d'Or winner is arguably his most controversial film, touching on deeply nuanced topics and never offering an easy moral way out. But it is in this nuance that Fjord thrives, with Sebastian Stan and Renate Reinsve delivering perfectly detailed performances that capture both the best and worst of these troubled characters and their terrifying situation.

The front-runner to take home the Academy's biggest prize is Christopher Nolan's historical epic The Odyssey, dubbed an "unrivaled cinematic spectacle" in Joe Schmidt's review for Collider. This famous tale's star-studded retelling hasn't been without its detractors, but those with a say have made it clear their love for The Odyssey, placing it firmly at the #1 spot in many people's predictions.

In fact, The Odyssey could very well overtake Ryan Coogler's Sinners as the most nominated film of all time, considering its sure impact in both the major and craft categories. Nolan delivers his typically ambitious scale and scope to one of history's grandest stories, culminating in a final thirty minutes that are, without doubt, some of the most encapsulating cinema of the decade so far. Could The Odyssey sail to a record-breaking Oscars night? All will be revealed in a few months.

#3405. This Bose Portable Bluetooth Speaker Is 33% Off Right Now

Pradershika Sharma is a tech deals writer for Lifehacker. She has a Master’s degree in English Literature, a B.Ed., and a TESOL certification. She has been writing professionally since 2018, creating product reviews, affiliate articles, and search ads for global clients while working with Rubix Agency and Cognizant. Previously, she spent a year teaching English at the junior high level.An avid reader since childhood, Pradershika's idea of extreme sports is staying up to read “just one more chapter.” She lives in India.

A price drop always stands out more when the product in question already has a reputation for delivering above its size, and that’s the case with the Bose SoundLink Plus. It hasn’t been on the market for long, but it’s already earned strong reviews—CNET labeled it “the Goldilocks of Bose Bluetooth speakers.” And right now, ahead of Black Friday, it’s down to $179 from $269, which price trackers show is the lowest it’s ever been.

Bose positions it right in the middle of the SoundLink lineup, and you feel that balance in how it’s built. It’s compact enough to clip onto a backpack using its built-in nylon strap, and tough enough to handle getting knocked around, and sealed against dust and full water submersion with an IP67 rating. Battery life can last up to 20 hours, depending on the volume, which is sufficient for full-day outings. On the connectivity side, there’s Bluetooth 5.4 with AAC and AptX Adaptive support, as well as the ability to keep two devices paired for smoother switching. What you don’t get is a microphone, an aux port, or any voice assistant support, which is worth considering if you prefer wired options or use speakers for calls.

As for its sound profile, it leans into mid- and high-bass, which gives electronic and pop tracks a lively pulse, though at higher volumes, you may notice some compression (which is common in speakers this size). It also doesn’t reach into true low-bass territory, so anyone who wants thumping sub-bass may not get it here, but the punch it does deliver feels clean for its size, notes this PCMag review. And while you won't get the width and separation of a stereo mix since the SoundLink Plus plays audio in mono, its directivity is good—meaning its sound remains clear from different listening positions, so you don't have to sit directly in front of it to get a good experience.

#3402. Eight 'Winter Arc' Rules That Will Actually Deliver Results

There are a lot of terrible social media trends out there aimed at self-improvement, yet even though everybody has been making fun of the "Winter Arc" craze, I actually think it’s a good one. During your Winter Arc, you promise yourself you’ll stick to your fitness and self-care routines during (and despite) the end-of-year chaos. It's a good goal, with one caveat: Make sure you choose rules that will actually improve your life and deliver results.

Think of the “arc” in the sense of a “story arc.” The Winter Arc is a self-improvement journey that unfolds over the last few months of the calendar year. The most hardcore #gymtok-ers will tell you the Winter Arc officially begins on Oct. 1, but others start in early November, or whenever they get around to it. The "when" isn't critical, though—whenever you read this is a fine time to start. The close of the Winter Arc is fixed, however: It ends Jan. 1, just as everybody who is less dedicated than you is waking from their holiday food comas and resolving to get in shape.

You get to choose your own terms for your Winter Arc. The general vibe is one of locking in, committing to your goals, and actually doing the things you’re always saying you’ll do. TikToker @carlyupgraded has said that her own mental image of someone nailing their Winter Arc is “hood up, headphones on, getting ready to go for a run in the rain at 5 a.m.”

It turns out I’ve accidentally been Winter-Arc-ing for years; I just didn’t know it had a catchy name. Why save your gym routine for New Year’s when you’ll have the place to yourself all December? We’re even gifted with an extra hour in the mornings to fill with something productive.

I really love the mindset shift involved. Commonly, people are active in the summer (great time for outdoor fun), may or may not stick with their routines in the fall, and let everything fall apart as the holidays approach. Who has time to go to the gym when you’re planning Thanksgiving, attending holiday parties, studying for final exams, or whatever else the end of the year throws in front of you?

But that’s the exact reason why this time of year is the best to start (or restart) a fitness routine, or really any kind of routine. When you start a routine during a busy time of year, you’ll be forced to make it sustainable. The gym routine you can stick with amid the chaos isn’t going to be one you drop after a few months. You’re already training yourself to work around obstacles as they come up, which is a key component of self-efficacy. And when the chaos clears on Jan. 1, your routine will be even easier to stick to.

Of course, there are ways to lean in too hard: Choosing unsustainable habits, falling for bad diet advice, mistaking not masturbating for some kind of health hack, the usual suspects. There’s also the pitfall of focusing too much on the vibes and too little on what you’re actually going to do or how you’ll benefit.

And then there’s the framing: You were working on yourself all year, but you’re in danger of letting up on the gas, but you’re committed to locking in so that you’re a step ahead of everybody who takes this time to slack off. I really don’t love this tack. Self-improvement is not a competition. There’s a difference between being consistent in your training and healthy eating (good) and seeing the pursuit of health and fitness as something where you always have to work harder because you’re at risk of getting left behind.

I also don’t love how gendered the Winter Arc TikToks tend to be. When you search for Winter Arc content, the first few suggestions include “winter arc for women” and “winter arc for men.” When I first started looking at the Winter Arc trend a few years ago, the women’s versions were more likely to include restrictive dieting or to focus on how the Winter Arc will finally (sigh) snatch your waist. These days, the focus is more on personal goal setting: Lots of the girlies filming their Winter Arc rules are doing so in a notebook and talking about journaling exercises that will help you identify what you need to work on to get to your "best self." Sometimes this is all monetized; training plans and journaling prompts can, of course, be purchased at the link in bio.

I do like that many of the women’s versions emphasize sustainability and setting your own goals rather than copying somebody else's. I don't love the enormity of the mental burden you're supposed to shoulder before even beginning. Should I really have to file an in-depth written report with myself before revamping every area of my life with a 100% commitment to multiple goals?

The men’s versions tend to go off the rails in another direction, with rules like “no girls” or “go ghost.” No distractions! Here, I've seen a shift over the years as well: at first there was overly serious content, followed quickly by satire (yelling at the viewer to get divorced and go work out in the dark). Now the men's videos tend to be more vibes-based, featuring images of pre-dawn workouts and plates full of salad with motivational quotes playing in the background. When the men give their rules, they tend to be simpler than the women's—no journaling exercises—but they often boil down to the same overly strict routines. (And then, of course, they'll offer to sell you a 90-day or 60-day plan.)

If you’re going to do a Winter Arc (or if you’re already doing one), make sure to structure it in a way that benefits you. Choosing 10 overly ambitious goals and setting yourself up for failure is not a healthy way to approach self-improvement, OK? Pick goals that are meaningful, achievable without divine intervention, and trackable with tools you already have at hand (for example, tracking your steps with a Fitbit or your running mileage with a Garmin watch).

It’s also helpful to think of developing yourself over this arc, rather than taking it as a three-month (or two-month) challenge where you have to do everything right all the time. If you currently wake up at 8 a.m. and want to wake up at 5 a.m., you don’t have to set your alarm for 5 a.m. tomorrow. It’s OK to aim for 7:30 a.m., make that a habit, then try for 7:00 a.m., and so on.

With that in mind, here are some "rules" I've seen from creators that I'm actually on board with (so long as you don't overwhelm yourself with them):

Wake up earlier. A great goal, especially if you take advantage of the time change to make things easier on your body.

Get to bed on time. Never a bad idea. Cultivating good sleep habits in general is always worthwhile.

Get your steps in. Be thoughtful about what your target is: 10,000 is not for everybody. Better to choose a number that would be a modest improvement on what you already do.

Exercise X times per week. Pick a number that works for you, and get into it. Be realistic about your goal, and for the best results, be consistent even if you’re sore at first.

Eat healthy. This is a great goal, with the major caveat that there are a lot of ways to eat healthy. You don’t need to cut out sugar or pretend that there’s something evil about seed oils. Do get more protein and veggies.

Be more thoughtful about using social media. I’m not going to tell you to delete all your apps (“except TikTok,” as the TikTokers say). But it’s fair to consider whether you might want to delete a few apps, turn off some notifications, or put your phone on Do Not Disturb for more hours of the day.

Journal or read more. Journaling can be great for working through your feelings or cultivating a creative habit. Reading can be entertainment or a great way to learn. Choose whichever you need most.

Learn a new skill. I’ve mostly seen this one in the men’s TikToks, and I love it. They’re often thinking of “skills” that will help in some kind of entrepreneurship grift they’re about to sell you, but there are tons of skills that will come in handy in life, or that are at least fun to learn. Practice a language, get better at cooking, make some art. Skills are, as I’ve noted, a multi-layered exercise for your brain. And they may come in handy someday.

This year I've slacked off on my fitness routine as I've gotten more involved in other hobbies, but I'm actually looking forward to being more consistent. My winter goals include exercising early in the day when possible and reading 20 minutes each day. (I'm even tracking the second one with a sticker chart.)

Ana María's mother Angelica and sister Angie wrote in the fundraiser's description ... "At just 24 years old, Ana María Ramírez Cetina had a lifetime of dreams ahead of her. #3397. iOS 27.3 brings the iPhone Duo’s revamped StandBy to other iPhones

Apple released iOS 27.3 beta 1 today, with a surprisingly extensive set of new features and improvements across the system. One of them is the expansion of the iPhone Duo’s redesigned StandBy experience to other iPhone models. Here are the details.

When Apple announced the iPhone Duo, one of its exclusive new features was a redesigned StandBy experience with new clock faces and expanded customization options.

StandBy mode was introduced with iOS 17, and it essentially turns the iPhone into a smart display when placed horizontally while charging.

Until now, users of other iPhone models were limited to the original StandBy experience, which offered clock, widget, and photo views, but lacked the additional faces and more extensive customization options introduced with the iPhone Duo.

With iOS 27.3, however, Apple is extending the redesigned Analog and Digital Clock faces to other iPhones, with additional options for customizing their colors and complications. In addition to the new Calendar and Weather faces, the update adds support for Shared Albums to the Photos face, letting users choose which shared photos appear in StandBy.

Users with an iPhone 11 or later can now also create multiple versions of the same StandBy face, each with its own customization options, and swipe between them.

iOS 27.3 is expected to launch in December. To learn more about StandBy and how to customize its different faces, follow this link.

#3395. The 6 Best DC Movie Opening Shots, Ranked

Feel free to connect with him or check out his work. He's everywhere — Upwork, YouTube, Spotify, SoundCloud, Collider, LinkedIn, Instagram.

Opening shots are absolutely crucial in movies. They’re meant to hook you into the story instantly and establish the core rules and tone of everything that follows. And if the filmmakers get it right, they know the audience is theirs for the next two hours. That’s exactly why an opening is usually one of the best sequences in any movie.

And a good opening is even more important for the superhero genre, which is built on scale and spectacle. The genre has consistently delivered banger openings year after year, and DC has had more than its fair share. Today, we’re sifting through the DC movies and bringing you some of the greatest openings they’ve ever delivered.

A lot of people praise the opening sequence where Batman (Robert Pattinson) reflects on his second year as a vigilante in a rain-soaked, crime-ridden Gotham City on Halloween night. But that’s not how the movie opens. It actually opens with a claustrophobic POV of a masked figure, breathing heavily, stalking a family through binoculars. At first, you think it’s Batman scouting a criminal. Then a young boy comes out dressed in a red ninja costume, practicing martial arts moves with a toy sword, and you go, oh no, is that Bruce Wayne? Are they doing his parents’ murder again? Then you realize it’s none of those things.

It was actually the Riddler’s POV (Paul Dano), and you’d been watching him stalk his first victim, the Mayor of Gotham. These subtle misdirections, one after another, were so damn good. Then the Riddler steps out of the shadows, murders the Mayor in cold blood, and wraps his face in tape. This wasn’t the huge spectacle opening we’ve come to expect from the superhero genre. But it perfectly established the film’s slow-burn psychological horror tone and painted Gotham as a city drowning in crime and corruption, where not even the Mayor is safe in his own home.

Watchmen opens in an alternate-history 1985 with the murder of an aging vigilante called the Comedian (Jeffrey Dean Morgan). It’s filmed in Zack Snyder’s hallmark slow-motion style and meticulously choreographed to Nat King Cole’s “Unforgettable.” The Comedian is alone in his high-rise New York apartment when a mysterious, super-strong intruder breaks in, and the two erupt into a fierce hand-to-hand fight.

The Comedian is absolutely overpowered. The apartment gets destroyed. And blood flies through the air and splatters perfectly across a yellow smiley-face pin resting on his counter, recreating the iconic imagery from the comics. The sequence ends with the attacker throwing Blake through a glass window and sending him plummeting to the pavement below, which sets up the murder mystery that drives the entire movie.

Superman opens in the most comic book way it possibly could. We’re in the Antarctic snow, and a timeline of on-screen text walks you through the new DCU and Superman’s (David Corenswet) story so far. Three centuries ago, the first metahumans appeared. Three decades ago, Clark arrived on Earth. Three years ago, he revealed himself to the world as Superman. Three hours ago, the Hammer of Boravia attacked. And three minutes ago, Superman lost a battle for the first time.

It establishes the stakes so much better than any origin montage or fight sequence ever could. Usually, you’d establish the status quo, and then move to the conflict where Superman loses his first fight. But James Gunn straight up opens the movie with its aftermath! Immediately after, Superman crash-lands in the snow, bloody, whistling for Krypto while the Superman theme swells up behind him, and it instantly hypes you up for the rest of the movie.

Four of the largest communities on the planet, and four completely different reasons to belong to one. Here is yours, what it would give you, and the argument you would be having within a week.

You belong to the fandom that is really about comfort. Hogwarts works on people because it is a place rather than a plot, and the pull is not the wizard war so much as the corridors, the food, the weather and the sense that somebody is expecting you.

You belong to the deepest fandom on this list, the one where somebody has always read further than you and is quietly delighted to say so. Middle-earth rewards patience more than any other world in popular culture.

You belong to the loudest and largest tent of the four, the one where three generations are all watching the same thing and none of them agree about any of it. That disagreement is not a flaw in this fandom, it is the main activity.

You belong to the thinking fandom, the one that turns up for the argument rather than the explosion. Trek has always been a series of ethical problems in space, and the people who love it love being asked what they would have done.

The Dark Knight Rises opens at thousands of feet in the air with Bane (Tom Hardy) sitting in a CIA plane, hooded and chained. But you quickly realize he’s not a prisoner. He let himself get caught on purpose, because he needed to extract a high-value target who also happened to be on this plane. The CIA agent asks what the next step of his master plan is, and Bane looks up and calmly says, “Crashing this plane... with no survivors!” Suddenly, a massive transport plane drops out of the sky above them. Four mercenaries rappel down and rip the CIA plane in half. And they just hold it there, nose down, hanging from their own plane.

Shootouts and fistfights break out inside the cabin, and Bane manages to kill them all. And then, he even goes so far as to leave one of his own men behind so the body count matches the flight manifest. Bane escapes with his target and the rest of his team out the back of the fuselage as the plane breaks apart and crashes into the mountains. Christopher Nolan used real aircraft and practical stunt work, so it obviously looks insanely good. But it also establishes Bane as someone Batman (Christian Bale) has never really faced before, a villain who’s just as smart as he is, and a lot stronger.

The movie’s very first shot starts on a puddle’s reflection in a prison yard and tilts up to show Savant (Michael Rooker). He’s bouncing a rubber ball off the walls and floor with pinpoint accuracy, hitting marked “X” targets, and the ball lands right back in his hand. A small yellow canary flies into his cell, and Savant purposely bounces the ball around the room one last time, striking and killing the bird.

From there, Amanda Waller (Viola Davis) recruits him, and the movie transitions to the hilarious plane sequence where the squad of misfits meets each other for the first time. And it leads to the iconic bait-and-switch in Corto Maltese, where almost every character is wiped out in the first 10 minutes. It was completely unexpected, and it quickly established that this wasn’t going to be your typical superhero story and that no one was safe.

The Dark Knight begins with one of the best heist sequences ever filmed. The camera zooms into a glass skyscraper, a window shatters from the inside, and two men in clown masks use a zip-line to launch themselves across to the roof of Gotham National Bank. Meanwhile, a van screeches up to a street corner, where a man holding a clown mask is waiting. He hops in, and the men inside start talking about the man who planned the heist, the one they call Joker (Heath Ledger).

The crew storms the bank and begins the heist, but they also start methodically taking each other out, just like they’ve been ordered. Each one thinks he’s removing the weak link so there’s a bigger share for everyone else. None of them knows someone else is ready to take them out too. It continues until there’s just one of them left, and the getaway driver arrives in a school bus and shoots the last guy, revealing himself to be the Joker. He places a smoke grenade tied to a pin in the bank manager’s mouth, steps onto the school bus filled with millions of dollars in mob money, and pulls out into a line of identical school buses as the police sirens approach. It’s widely considered one of the greatest openings of all time across any genre.

#3394. Your Android Can Get Hacked Without You Doing Anything at All

You probably know that clicking suspicious links online or opening attachments from strangers in an email or text is a recipe for hacking. It's a dangerous world out there online, so it's always important to be vigilant. However, the danger doesn't always involve something you do. There are ways to hack your devices without requiring any intervention on your part whatsoever—and one such example is likely plaguing your Android device right now.

As reported by The Hacker News, there is a critical Android security flaw that could enable remote code execution on your device. In other words, bad actors could use the flaw to run their own code on your phone, effectively taking over the device for their own gain. The flaw, identified as CVE-2026-58868, isn't universal, but it is widespread: It currently affects Android 14 through Android 17, the latest version of Google's OS. If your phone runs Android 12 or Android 13, it may be unaffected, as Google doesn't identify these versions in its security bulletin, but it doesn't explicitly rule them out, either.

There are two silver linings here, however. One, Google hasn't confirmed any active exploits for this security flaw. While that isn't a guarantee that bad actors have missed this exploit so far, it at least opens that possibility. As such, there may be time for users to patch their devices before hackers truly take advantage of the flaw. Second, Google does have a patch for the flaw. The patch may not be available to you right away, however, as it's up to both the manufacturer of your phone and your carrier to issue these updates. Still, a patch is, at the very least, on its way.

This flaw is perhaps the most important to fix, but it's not the only serious issue. In all, Google's latest bulletin highlights 216 vulnerabilities, and, of those, 23 are "critical." As The Hacker News explains, two other of those critical flaws could also allow remote code execution when exploited.

To see whether the patch is installed on your end, open the Settings app on your phone, tap "About phone" or "About tablet," then choose the Android version on-screen. Look for a date of "2026-11-01" or later. All security patches from Nov. 1 and on will fix this issue. If not, you'll ned to wait for the patch.

Apple initially introduced ChatGPT integration in Xcode 26, followed by Anthropic’s Claude. Then, in Xcode 26.3, the company expanded both integrations with agentic coding capabilities through OpenAI’s Codex and Anthropic’s Claude Agent.

With Xcode 27, Apple added support for Google Gemini, alongside a redesigned interface, interactive planning, and multi-turn conversations.

Now, with Xcode 27.3, Apple is expanding the list of supported AI coding tools once again, this time adding GitHub Copilot.

The Xcode 27.3 beta 1 release notes include the following under the Coding Intelligence section:

As with the other agentic integrations, this is particularly good news for developers whose companies have standardized on GitHub Copilot, as they can now use their company’s preferred AI coding tool directly within Xcode.

Here are the full release notes for Xcode 27.3 beta 1:

Xcode 27.3 beta includes Swift 6.4 and SDKs for iOS 27.3, iPadOS 27.3, tvOS 27.3, watchOS 27.3, macOS 27.3, and visionOS 27.3. Xcode 27.3 beta supports on-device debugging in iOS 17 and later, tvOS 17 and later, watchOS 10 and later, and visionOS. Xcode 27.3 beta requires a Mac running macOS Tahoe 26.6 or later.

See Xcode Support to learn more about compatible platforms and deployment targets.

Mini PC or all-in-one? Here’s how Apple’s M6 desktops stack up

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

If you’re looking for a new computer and want a Mac, your first instinct might be to pick up one of the best MacBooks. However, opting for Apple’s premium laptops or even the much more affordable MacBook Neo has its drawbacks — especially if you're paying a portability premium for a machine that will rarely leave your desk.

Sure, the new MacBook Pro OLED looks fantastic with that illuminated Apple logo on the lid, and it is the first Mac with a touchscreen. For the majority of people, though, it’s total overkill. Unless you plan on editing 8K video or running demanding local AI models on the go, you’re buying far more computer than you need.

If you just want a reliable, fast Mac to use at home, Apple’s desktops are a much better bet. The powerhouse Mac Studio will be overkill for most, too. That’s why, if you’re setting up a dedicated home office or just need a shared family machine for the living room, the new Mac mini and iMac with Apple’s M6 chips make a whole lot more sense.

While you can configure either with beefier specs, I’ll be focusing on the entry-level models for this comparison: the base Mac mini with M6 and the base iMac with M6. The latest Mac mini landed in September of 2026, followed shortly by the new iMac in November. Since both sport the latest Apple Silicon, either will easily last you for years to come.

Having reviewed both the Mac mini M6 and the iMac M6, the question is: which one actually deserves a spot on your desk and is worth your hard-earned cash? Here’s a full breakdown of their real-world performance, design, ergonomics, and value to help you decide between one of the best mini PCs and one of the best all-in-one computers you can buy right now.

2 x USB-C, 3.5mm headphone jack (front), 3 x Thunderbolt 4/USB 4, 1 x HDMI, 1 x 2.5 gigabit Ethernet (back)

2 x Thunderbolt 4, 1 x 3.5mm headphone jack

Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, Thread, Gigabit Ethernet

Even though the Mac mini with M6 and iMac with M6 are new Apple desktops, they share one very important thing in common: neither sports a radical redesign. Instead, they feature almost identical designs to their predecessors.

The Mac mini was completely redesigned back in 2024 with the Mac mini M4. Like that machine, this new model is much more compact at 5 x 5 x 2 inches and retains those front ports — specifically two USB-C ports and a 3.5mm headphone jack. Besides charging, you can use those front ports to quickly connect your iPhone to transfer data, and having a headphone jack on the front means you can use wired headphones without having to plug them in at the back.

Sign up to the Tom's iGuide weekly newsletter with coverage on everything from product launches to software updates, this is your go-to source for the latest updates on all the best Apple content.

Then around back on the Mac mini M6, you get three Thunderbolt 4 ports, an HDMI port, a Gigabit Ethernet port, and a power port. Those Thunderbolt ports are great if you want to use one of Apple’s first-party monitors like the Studio Display or Studio Display XDR, but they also work with most portable monitors. Meanwhile, the Mac mini M6’s HDMI port is ideal for traditional monitors without a USB-C port.

The iMac with M6’s design is even older, though, as Apple first introduced it back in 2021 with the iMac M1. Though it has a much larger footprint than the Mac mini, the iMac M6 is still quite compact for an all-in-one at 21.5 x 18.1 x 5.8 inches.

Given the iMac M6 is an all-in-one, you don’t get nearly as many ports as you do on the Mac mini since you don’t need to hook it up to a separate monitor. While my review unit has four ports, on the base model, you just get two Thunderbolt 4 ports.

Then on the left edge of the device, there’s a 3.5mm headphone jack and that’s it. You can get an Ethernet port on its power adapter, but you’ll have to pay extra for it. The iMac M6 also features a six-speaker system and a built-in 12MP Center Stage camera for video calls.

Overall, you can’t go wrong with either the Mac mini or the iMac when it comes to their respective designs. Both desktops look sleek, but if you want a computer with the smallest footprint and the most ports, the Mac mini is the better choice. You will have to bring your own display, webcam, and other accessories, though.

Although the latest Mac mini and iMac both sport Apple’s new M6 chips, there is a slight difference between them when it comes to the base models.

While the Mac mini has an M6 chip with 12 CPU and 12 GPU cores, the M6 chip in the iMac only has 10 of each. In my testing, both machines feel quite snappy for everyday tasks like opening apps and browsing the web thanks to the improved efficiency that comes with the 2nm process Apple used with its M6 chips. It’s with more demanding tasks where you’ll notice a difference.

For instance, if you’re editing a lot of photos, rendering video, or are a power user with dozens of browser tabs open simultaneously, then the more powerful M6 chip in the Mac mini will certainly make a difference. If you just want a Mac for watching videos, writing emails, and basic daily tasks, the difference between these two M6 chips will be negligible.

One other area where you will definitely see an impact though is with gaming. While neither of these Macs can serve as a replacement for one of the best gaming PCs, they’re surprisingly capable when it comes to gaming and this is especially true with older titles. Here, the two extra GPU cores in the Mac mini help keep frame rates smoother.

For those who plan on pushing their new Apple desktop to the limit or playing games on it, then the more powerful M6 chip in the Mac mini is the better choice. However, if you just need a reliable machine for day-to-day use, the 10-core M6 in the base iMac has plenty of power to get the job done.

If you opt for a Mac mini over an iMac, you’re obviously going to need to get a monitor to go along with it — or you could use one you already have, just like with your mouse and keyboard, to bring your total overall cost down. However, if you want an excellent display with a high pixel count without having to do a ton of research first, there’s no screen quite like the one on the iMac.

The iMac features a 24-inch, 4.5K display with a resolution of 4480 x 2520. Since this panel is manufactured specifically for Apple, you won’t find another standalone monitor on the market with that exact screen size, resolution, and pixel density.

Most monitors that deliver around 218 pixels per inch like the iMac cost as much or more than a Mac mini M6 on their own. Samsung’s 27-inch ViewFinity S9 runs around $800 to $1,000, while LG’s 27-inch UltraFine 5K costs around $1,000 to $1,200. Granted, those panels are slightly larger than 24 inches, but they demand a hefty premium.

If you want something larger and more affordable, 27-inch 4K panels like the Dell UltraSharp or Asus ProArt can be had for around $400 to $500. However, because they aren’t native Apple displays, you do miss out on native features — like using the brightness keys on a Magic Keyboard to dim the screen without third-party software.

Even though 24 inches might sound modest, the high pixel density of the iMac gives you plenty of usable canvas. In my testing with the iMac M6, I was able to comfortably work with two browser windows side by side without feeling cramped.

There is one big catch with the iMac, though: ergonomics. Unlike the Studio Display or Pro Display XDR, there is no height-adjustable stand option. The built-in stand only tilts about 5 degrees forward or 25 degrees back.

To get your iMac to a proper ergonomic height — where your eyes naturally align just below the top third of the panel — you’ll likely need to set it on a monitor riser or desk shelf. Alternatively, you can ditch the stand altogether at checkout and order the factory VESA mount version, though you'll need to budget for one of the best monitor arms alongside your new all-in-one.

If you want a massive display, dual or even triple-monitor flexibility, or full control over your desk layout, the Mac mini is the obvious choice. But if you want a compact, incredibly sharp screen built right into the machine, the iMac’s display is tough to beat.

As the Mac mini doesn’t give you that computer-in-a-box experience that the iMac does, there’s a whole host of optional 3rd-party accessories available for it. From stands and hubs that sit underneath to enclosures that rest on top to add extra ports and even M.2 SSD slots for expanded storage, you can really accessorize Apple’s smallest Mac to your heart’s desire.

You’ll find a few USB hubs and add-ons for the iMac, but nowhere near as many as you will for the Mac mini. One new accessory I’m looking forward to testing with the iMac M6 is BenQ’s iScreenBar, a monitor light bar designed specifically to match the color and aluminum aesthetic of Apple’s all-in-one.

Likewise, Satechi makes a slim dock that sits directly over the iMac’s base to add front-facing ports and an SSD slot — similar to its popular stand and hub for the Mac mini. It’s a clean setup, but overall, the 3rd-party accessory ecosystem for the iMac remains much smaller, and for obvious reasons: there's just less to add to an all-in-one.

When it comes to first-party upgrades from Apple, you can configure both machines with extra unified memory and internal storage. Keep in mind that because everything is soldered down, these upgrades have to be chosen at checkout when ordering through Apple’s website — you can't crack either machine open to upgrade them later.

The most unique upgrade for the iMac M6 is Apple’s nano-texture glass. Just like on high-end MacBooks, instead of standard glossy glass that catches reflections, you can pay an extra $200 at checkout to add a matte finish. The catch? Apple doesn't offer nano-texture on the base 10-core iMac. You have to step up to the higher-tier model first before tacking on that $200 display upgrade, which widens the price gap between it and the Mac mini considerably. Still, there’s no other all-in-one on the market that offers a matte display quite like it.

If you want a vast ecosystem of desk mounts, docks, and external drives to completely personalize your workstation, the Mac mini is the obvious choice. But if you work in a sunlit room with nearby windows and glare constantly drives you crazy, stepping up to an iMac with nano-texture glass might be worth the extra investment.

Although the Mac mini M4 could be had for $599 at launch, thanks to RAMaggedon and the ongoing component crunch, Apple bumped up the starting price of the new Mac mini M6 to $899. As a result, when you factor in the cost of a display, keyboard, mouse, webcam, and speakers, the Mac mini is suddenly playing in the exact same price bracket as the iMac.

The iMac M6 saw a price increase of its own. While the iMac M4 started at $1,299, the new M6-powered version climbs to $1,499. The Mac mini used to be an unbeatable bargain compared to the rest of Apple’s lineup, but if you don’t already have a desk full of peripherals at home, you could easily spend $1,350 to $1,450 just to get a setup comparable to the iMac.

The real value proposition between the two comes down to your existing hardware. If you already have a spare monitor, keyboard, and mouse sitting on your desk, the Mac mini M6 delivers better raw performance for significantly less cash. But if you’re starting completely from scratch, the iMac’s $1,499 sticker price includes a built-in 4.5K display, crisp speakers, a 12MP Center Stage camera, and a color-matched Magic Keyboard and Magic Mouse right in the box.

If this is your first dedicated desktop, the iMac is the easier, better-value buy — unless you prefer an à la carte approach where you handpick every screen, dock, and keyboard yourself. If total customization is the goal, or you already have the accessories to make it work, go with the Mac mini instead.

While you can’t go wrong with either the Mac mini M6 or the iMac M6, the choice between the two ultimately comes down to how complicated you want your desk setup to be.

Let’s say you just moved and need to get to work right away in a new apartment where space is at a premium. One trip to the Apple Store later, you have a complete desktop in a box that you can set up in less than 30 minutes. If you want to heavily personalize your workspace, however — or if you prefer a much larger display or even multiple screens — then the Mac mini makes far more sense.

Regardless of which entry-level Apple desktop you choose, make sure you know what you’ll be using it for and how demanding your workflow will be before hitting checkout. When it comes to their internal components, neither the Mac mini M6 nor the iMac M6 can be upgraded after the fact. It’s essential that you configure the right chip, memory, and storage the first time around.

Although I review mini PCs for a living and have always been a big fan of the Mac mini, setting up and testing the iMac gave me a whole new appreciation for its simplicity. Sometimes, there is undeniable value in not having to overthink your monitor, cables, and peripherals.

#3387. 'Ocarina of Time' for Switch 2 Might Already Have a Weird Glitch

Thursday is a big day for Zelda fans. That's when the remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time officially launches on Switch 2, marking the first major linear (i.e., non-open-world) 3D Zelda game since the 2016 Twilight Princess remake on Wii U. I, for one, have been waiting for this day for years. I loved the N64 original and the 3DS remake, so to have the chance to play a modern take on the definitive Zelda is so exciting—that is, if it actually runs as it should.

I stumbled upon this interesting post on X from Austin John Plays, a YouTuber with a host of Zelda coverage. According to Austin John Plays, Ocarina of Time already ships with a weird glitch that won't necessarily break your experience, but which may slow it down for a while, and perhaps even confuse players into thinking something is wrong with their game or their console.

As his post explains, if you're playing the physical copy of Ocarina of Time, and it's the first game you've ever played on your Switch 2—maybe you got one of those fancy new Zelda anniversary consoles and want to break it in properly?—you may run into glaring performance issues: The game may freeze, your controller may stop working, and the FPS may drop to single digits.

Luckily, Austin John Plays says the fix is easy: just wait. Eventually, your game will boot back to the title screen. When it does, don't try to play right away. Instead, close the game, restart your Switch 2, then try relaunching Ocarina of Time. Austin John Plays advises you may need to repeat this process two or three times, but after that, you shouldn't continue to run into issues. I wouldn't be surprised if Nintendo releases a patch right away for this glitch if it turns out to be as widespread as this post implies.

However, seeing as the game doesn't come out until tomorrow, there's something you can do to prevent it. Austin John Plays thinks the bug only impacts Switch 2 consoles that haven't run other games before. If you've had your console a while, you're likely set. But if you just bought the 40th anniversary Zelda edition of the Switch 2, you might not have had a chance to run a game on it yet. As such, download a game from the e-shop—even a free demo—just to get the system running. Hopefully, that will be enough to circumvent the glitch, and prevent issues when Ocarina of Time launches tomorrow.

'The Mean Season" is a sun-drenched, stormy mystery set against 1980s Miami

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

While I'd usually queue up the holiday movies as the season approaches, for some reason, I'm not quite ready this year. I miss long summer days, even if they do come with insects and heat. Like me, if you are longing for beachy days, you may want to skip the queue of winter-heavy movies and opt for a summer-based thriller instead.

I happened upon "The Mean Season" on Tubi while looking for a thriller, and it completely swept me away. Starring Kurt Russell, Mariel Hemingway, and Richard Jordan, the film is set in a stormy, beautiful Miami during its "mean season" of storms and hurricanes.

It let me put off the cold weather a little longer while keeping me captivated by an intricate serial-killer plot — the ultimate escape from the dark fall and winter days to come. And best of all, it's completely free to stream "The Mean Season" since it's on Tubi.

"The Mean Season" kicks off with a murder. Alongside shots of a newspaper's printing press, a woman is seen walking out to the beach. At first, she seems to smile, only for someone to come up behind her, pointing a gun. The camera cuts away to a looming storm as a gunshot rings out.

The next scene introduces us to the weary Malcolm Anderson (Kurt Russell), who is ready to leave behind his journalism career in Miami for a slower life with his girlfriend, Christine Connelly (Mariel Hemingway), in Colorado. But before he leaves, his editor, Bill Nolan (Richard Masur), approaches him with one final assignment: a body that's been found.

The victim turns out to be a teenage girl. Malcolm is on the scene, talking to witnesses and gathering information, then returns to the office to write up the article. After it gets printed, he gets a phone call. While initially thinking it was a prank or a strange reader, the caller (Richard Jordan) admits to being the one who killed the girl. He even shares details only the killer would know.

Thus begins a truly bizarre relationship between reporter and murderer. The killer wants Malcolm to keep writing about him. Despite Malcolm's longing to escape the entire hustle for news, he can't help but stay and see it all play out. As the news reports on the crimes, the killer becomes restless, believing that too much focus is on Malcolm and not on the killer himself. It won't be long before both Malcolm and his girlfriend are at risk.

Sign up to the weekly Tom's Streaming Guide to stay in the loop with the latest releases and top recommendations across your favorite streaming services. We’ve got you covered with a complete guide on what’s worth watching.

While "The Mean Season" has its flaws, Russell and Jordan's excellent acting and the vivid Miami setting make it an electric thriller. These types of late '80s thrillers always leave me wanting more; it's something about the gritty setting and the less-than-combed look of the entire movie that makes it feel more real than anything of our modern era.

Plus, I've always loved Kurt Russell in films. He manages to portray a charming, decent man with notable personality flaws—including the ambition shown here that leads him into a relationship with a killer, putting both his and his girlfriend's lives at risk.

Richard Jordan as the killer is downright frighteningly good. He plays a diabolical man incredibly well, reminding me of how much we lost when this actor passed away far too soon. He's one of the biggest reasons to spend time watching this flick.

I also can't resist the Miami beach setting, especially with the stormy weather looming as equally close and threatening as the killer himself.

Also, keep an eye out for a fresh-faced Andy Garcia as Detective Ray Martinez. He does an excellent job matching the intensity of the moment throughout the movie.

#3384. Apple now explicitly bans employees from using confidential information in prediction markets

Apple has updated its insider trading policy to explicitly prohibit employees from using confidential information to bet on prediction markets. Here are the details.

Following yesterday’s fiscal Q4 2026 earnings report, Apple today published its fiscal 2026 Form 10-K, which is a mandatory annual filing with the SEC that provides a detailed look at the company’s finances, business, and risks.

Among the documents included in the filing is an updated version of Apple’s insider trading policy.

Until last year, Apple’s insider trading policy, filed with the SEC as Exhibit 19.1, included the following prohibitions:

However, the updated policy includes a new prohibition:

No Trading in Prediction Markets Based on Confidential Information. Do not participate in “prediction markets” or similar platforms to wager, bet, trade, buy or sell contracts based on the outcome of future events, or otherwise enter into event contracts, when such activity involves the use of Apple Confidential Information (as defined in Apple’s Business Conduct Policy) about Apple or any other company (including Apple suppliers, manufacturers, vendors or customers, such as cellular network carriers or other business partners) obtained in connection with your work at Apple. You must also not tip Apple Confidential Information to others who may participate in such markets. Apple Confidential Information includes, but is not limited to, material nonpublic information. This prohibition applies whether or not the activity constitutes insider trading or securities trading under applicable laws.

While much of this may seem obvious, how insider trading rules apply to prediction markets has been something of a gray area, to put it mildly. And while major prediciton markets explicitly ban the practice in their terms of service, enforcement remains a challenge.

In Apple’s case, the new language explicitly extends restrictions beyond traditional securities trading, making it clear that employees cannot use confidential information to place bets on prediction markets, even when those transactions don’t qualify as insider trading under applicable laws.

You can read Apple’s full 2026 Form 10-K on its Investor Relations page.

#3383. 10 Shows Like 'Phony' You Should Watch Next

Ross Johnson writes about television, film, and literature for Lifehacker. He has a degree in political science from the University of Rochester and has previously been a legal writer and editor for Thomson Reuters, for which he later traveled around India and the Middle East as an educator specializing in American English style and grammar for adults.

Ross has been an actor on stage, in commercials, and in independent films since childhood, and has written hundreds of articles and essays on genre literature and cinema for Barnes & Noble, Gizmodo, Kotaku, and Yahoo! Entertainment.Ross produces the Swan Songs film podcast and hosts The Sound of Tomorrow, a pop culture and current affairs radio show based in Rochester, New York, where he lives with his husband and dogs and supports the local arts and cinema scene. You can find him on Bluesky.

This is Streamalikes, where you can find a curated list of recommendations to stream based on what you already like.

What if you knew your mom wasn't really your mom, but no one believed you? That's the improbable but entertaining premise of Hulu's Phony, which stars Sam Nivola as a teenager who wakes up from a car accident and quickly comes to believe that his mother (Friday Night Lights' Connie Britton) is an imposter. Of course, no one believes him. I'm not sure I believe him, but it'll be pretty boring if it turns out that he just had a really bad concussion the whole time.

It's a coming-of-age drama and a surreal mystery with hints of comedy, and though it borrows elements from other shows, it stands apart for the skill with which it blends everything together. While you wait to see how the story plays out, here are 10 more twisted mysteries to stream now.

A twisty-turny (and well-reviewed) bit of fake identity folderol, Apple Cider Vinegar stars Kaitlyn Dever as Belle Gibson, a real-life Australian cancer survivor (except not really!) With a cheeky sense of humor and a willingness to distort reality, the show follows the wellness influencer as she fakes multiple cancer diagnoses in order to better market her alternative, MAHA-esque app and remedies to the unwitting. As her livelihood comes under threat, her lies grow more elaborate. Stream Apple Cider Vinegar on Netflix.

Alia Shawkat stars here as Dory Sief, an aimless millennial who decides, after seeing a missing-person poster for a college acquaintance, that she's going to make it her purpose to track her down—with the extremely begrudging support of her friends. But neither Chantal nor her disappearance are anything like what Dory expects. The show shifts focus from season to season. Initially a darkly comic take on a Nancy Drew-style mystery, it later finds the gang desperate to cover up a mostly unintentional murder, and getting in deeper each season. It's a funny, smart, and weird and shares talent with Phony in the form of writer/producer Anthony King, who serves as co-showrunner on the new series. Stream Search Party on Netflix.

This one's largely about adults, so it skips the coming-of-age angle central to Phony, but it has a quirky mystery, gaslighting, and a protagonist whose sanity is questioned by just about everyone all the same. This fun and very loose adaptation of the 1989 Tom Hanks film finds Keke Palmer's Samira and Jack Whitehall's Rob moving back to his impossibly safe and tidy hometown. Their house happens to be across the street from a dilapidated Victorian eyesore that may or may not have been the location of a murder a couple of decades before—a murder of a girl who made the mistake of trying to get away. As Samira adjusts to new motherhood and life on the cul-de-sac, she learns that even the nicest of her neighbors have secrets, and comes to suspect that her husband knows more about the missing girl than he's letting on. Stream The 'Burbs on Peacock.

When pretty, popular girl Kate Wallis (Olivia Holt) goes missing without a trace in 1993, awkward Jeanette Turner (Chiara Aurelia) steps in to fill the gap, modeling herself after Kate, working her way into the missing girl's social circle, and getting close with her boyfriend. That's all going great until Kate reappears two years later, accusing Jeanette of having witnessed the events around her disappearance and keeping quiet. Whoops. There's even more going on, as the show shifts back and forth between 1993, 1994, and 1995 to slowly reveal the missing pieces. Stream Cruel Summer on Hulu.

Based on a Harlan Coben novel, Fool Me Once is a bit more of a political thriller than a coming-of-age thing, but we're still in "what the hell is up with my family?" territory: Michelle Keegan plays Maya Stern, a former special ops pilot dealing with the murder of her husband, whom she then impossibly catches playing with their daughter on a nanny cam. The resulting mystery ties into the earlier death of her sister and leads to a web of conspiracy involving her husband's family and a shady pharmaceutical company. Stream Fool Me Once on Netflix.

A vibe match more than anything else, this dark and twisty mystery with a slightly surreal sense of humor also features a single mom who is definitely not what she appears to be. Kim Mo-mi (Lee Han-byeol, initially), the Mask Girl of the title, is a uniquely complicated woman; she always wanted to be a K-Pop idol, but it was always made clear to her that she's not nearly pretty enough for that kind of stardom. So, in order to fill that void, she's got a side hustle. On top of her boring office job, she puts on a blonde wig and a mask to perform as a camgirl for anonymous men. It's a means to express herself creatively and sexually with a level of control—until a mistake causes her to lose that control, a co-worker discovers her secret life, and desperation leads to murder. The show shifts perspectives continually, feeling most like Phony when it focuses on Mo-mi's daughter. Stream Mask Girl on Netflix.

Flipping things around a bit, albeit in a similar "am I just being paranoid?" vein, The Girlfriend deals with a mom who may or may not be freaking out for no reason. Starring Robin Wright as Laura Sanderson, a wealthy art gallery owner in London whose son (Laurie Davidson) brings home a new, working-class girlfriend, Cherry Laine (Olivia Cooke)—immediately strikes Laura as not-our-kind. But is there more to it? Can someone with the name "Cherry Laine" truly be trusted? There's definitely something off, and we're kept guessing as to whether or not this is the story of a dangerous con artist or an overbearing mom—or maybe a little of each. Stream The Girlfriend on Prime Video.

Coming from Irish playwright and Derry Girls creator Lisa McGee, this show eschews the relatively subtle dark comedy of Phony for something much more gloriously surreal. Three high school friends from Belfast reunite after learning that an estranged bestie has died unexpectedly—except that maybe she didn't; a mixed blessing given that they all have secrets that they were hoping would be buried with the maybe departed. Now they're off to investigate the mystery of the murder(?), which turns into a hunt for the friend that they only thought they knew, while inadvertently revealing plenty of secrets of their own. The tone is all over the place in a way that somehow works, with flashes of sincerity balancing out the comedy. Stream How to Get to Heaven From Belfast on Netflix.

Shin Hye-sun offers up a phenomenal performance as Sarah Kim (well: sort of), a wealthy businesswoman who is discovered, at the series' opening, under a sewer grate. The police detective charged to investigate quickly finds inconsistencies in the woman's identity, and after interviewing Sarah's friend and business associate, comes to feel that neither woman is exactly (or anything, like she seems. Though it takes itself more seriously than Phony, it's still an addictively twisty mystery built around a constructed identity. Stream The Art of Sarah on Netflix.

There's a lot going on in this steamy, telenovela-esque drama. Camila Román (Carolina Miranda) finally meets Fernando Castell (Rodolfo Salas), a Tinder match, in Las Vegas, and things get very hot very quickly—he's everything he seemed to be and then some. If anything, she's the sketchy one: a dancer, not a nurse as she said, and with a possessive ex following her around. Still, it's all going great until she decides to surprise Fernando after he flies back to Colombia (which: never do that), and gets a totally different dude when she asks for him at his work. And that's just the beginning! Stream Fake Profile on Netflix.

#3381. macOS 27.3 adds native Markdown rendering to Quick Look

Starting with macOS 27.3, users can preview Markdown files with proper formatting directly in Quick Look. Here are the details.

Apple released macOS 27.3 beta 1 today, with new Safari features, including Vertical Tabs and Adaptive Dark Mode, expanded Siri AI capabilities, and new tools for third-party developers.

Among the smaller changes coming to the Mac is a welcome improvement to Quick Look. As of macOS 27.3 beta 1, .md files are rendered with proper formatting directly in Quick Look, rather than displaying their raw Markdown syntax.

Apple has been expanding Markdown support across its platforms, including the ability to import and export Markdown files in Notes. Markdown has also become increasingly important with the rise of AI agents, which use .md files to store instructions, context, and other information.

In fact, as Federico Viticci noted today on X, Apple’s new Siri AI app skills feature also uses Markdown-based SKILL.md files, allowing developers to provide instructions that help Siri perform complex tasks within their apps.

What a journey for Markdown, @gruber The new Siri AI developer framework now officially uses skills, with specific Markdown guidance for SKILL .md agent files https://t.co/koi8K541le pic.twitter.com/TF72JJZRXc

For the uninitiated, Markdown is a simple text formatting syntax created by John Gruber in 2004, and has since become widely used for writing documentation, publishing content online (including this very post), and, more recently, providing instructions to AI agents.

Markdown is a text-to-HTML conversion tool for web writers. Markdown allows you to write using an easy-to-read, easy-to-write plain text format, then convert it to structurally valid HTML.

In practice, this means you can create headings, bold text, lists, and links using just a few simple characters. And, starting with macOS 27.3, you’ll be able to preview the results directly in Quick Look, without having to open the file in a separate app.

To learn more about Markdown, follow this link.
